items.streamTitle: Mouse experiments linked motor-memory decay to removal of learning-associated myelin
items.streamSummary: Mouse experiments showed microglial removal of motor-learning-associated myelin contributes to memory decay, with CD47 manipulation changing decay. Generalization to human knowledge or training retention is untested.
items.attribution: Hu, Luo, Zhou et al. — Nature Neuroscience (mouse causal neurobiology experiments; November 17, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Preschool children showed appearance-based peer preferences in controlled comparisons
items.streamSummary: In 139 children aged three to seven, controlled same-face image comparisons showed graded hypothetical peer preferences by visible dental condition. The result measures immediate appearance-based judgments, not actual friendships.
items.attribution: Benke, Zsido, Basler et al. — Scientific Reports (preschool choice experiment; November 17, 2026)

items.streamTitle: AI dependence predicted lower critical-thinking disposition across three teacher-training waves
items.streamSummary: A three-wave study of 461 Chinese pre-service teachers associated greater AI dependence with lower critical-thinking disposition; AI self-efficacy partially mediated and stress moderated one path. Observational associations are not causal effects.
items.attribution: Zhu, Yang, Long et al. — Scientific Reports (three-wave longitudinal survey; November 17, 2026)

items.streamTitle: LLM public-opinion estimates approximated aggregate surveys but distorted partisan distributions
items.streamSummary: Three studies benchmarked LLM estimates against Pew polling: some aggregate estimates approached survey distributions, but partisan bias, excessive homogeneity and inferior persona-aggregation threatened validity. LLM answers are not human survey observations.
items.attribution: Li, Wang, Xie et al. — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications (public-opinion benchmarking; November 17, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Open tract-level synthetic populations preserve demographic–health joint structure
items.streamSummary: SHAPE released open 2024 U.S. tract/county synthetic populations and validated health-related small-area estimates against CDC data. It is a reproducible population-data infrastructure, not a behavioral influence prediction model.
items.attribution: Von Hoene, Gupta, Von Hoene et al. — Scientific Data (SHAPE public dataset and GIS tools; November 17, 2026)

items.streamTitle: CSIS assessed PLA mission-command and joint-warfighting vulnerabilities behind modernization
items.streamSummary: A November 16 CSIS report argues that PLA modernization may mask vulnerabilities in command, joint operations, logistics, dynamic targeting and corruption. It is interview-informed operational assessment, not measured wartime performance.
items.attribution: Jones, Heginbotham and Byman — CSIS, Peace Disease: Is the PLA Battle Ready? (research report; November 16, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Video-detector research found periodic decoding signatures in many generated clips
items.streamSummary: A November 16 preprint detected periodic video-decoder traces across many generators and improved benchmark detector AUROC. The results concern synthetic-video classification, not verified operational detection or reduced influence.
items.attribution: Sun, Li, Mei and Shou — arXiv preprint, VAE Rhythm (generated-video forensics benchmark; November 16, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Continuous-time causal-graph theory characterized what can be learned under latent confounding
items.streamSummary: W-separation yields formal, testable equivalence classes for continuous-time causal graphs with hidden common causes. It advances identification theory but supplies no validated human intervention forecasts.
items.attribution: Kempf, Kilbertus and Manten — arXiv preprint (continuous-time causal-discovery theory; November 16, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Truthful fragments misled AI agents into unsupported narratives across rumor events
items.streamSummary: Across 1,090 rumor targets, AI agents often accepted misleading narratives assembled from truthful facts; checking direct support for inferred links improved accuracy. These are synthetic-agent findings, not human persuasion rates.
items.attribution: Hu, He, Huang et al. — arXiv preprint, Generative Montage (AI-agent narrative-evidence evaluation; November 16, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Latent attention improved prediction of social influence in 14 of 15 datasets
items.streamSummary: A probabilistic social-influence model added unobserved neighbor selection and opinion retention, improving held-out likelihood on 14 of 15 empirical datasets. Better fit does not by itself identify causal influence.
items.attribution: Thompson, Tian, Huynh et al. — arXiv preprint, Learning Social Influence with Unobserved Attention (methods and empirical evaluation; October 8, 2026)

items.streamTitle: Mental-state prompting helped empathetic AI responses, but factual grounding explained much of the gain
items.streamSummary: A November 16 dialogue-system study found mental-state-conditioned replies improved automated scores, but a factual dialogue-summary control performed similarly; modeled mental states and human empathy effects were not validated.
items.attribution: Hayoung Lee and Seonghee Lee — Scientific Reports (empathetic dialogue model evaluation, November 16)

items.streamTitle: Human-derived decision heuristics improved multi-agent simulation of the bullwhip effect
items.streamSummary: Across 231 Beer Game sessions with seven LLMs, cognitive grounding using qualitative human decision heuristics improved collective trajectory fit. The result supports task-specific calibration, not general synthetic-human fidelity.
items.attribution: Zhu and Heydari — Nature Computational Science (human-benchmark LLM-agent simulation analysis, November 16)

items.streamTitle: EU sanctions identified a state-directed information-manipulation organization
items.streamSummary: A November 16 Council decision sanctioned 30 people and two entities and identified the Social Design Agency as a Russian-directed FIMI operator. Official attribution and restrictions are not measured influence or deterrence outcomes.
items.attribution: Council of the European Union — official restrictive-measures announcement (November 16)

items.streamTitle: Hippocampal ultrasound disruption impaired inference from learned relationships
items.streamSummary: Human fMRI and a 20-person stimulation experiment linked hippocampal relational representations to flexible inference; disruption impaired inferred relationships but not preference learning. Transfer beyond the artificial game is untested.
items.attribution: Pan, D’Ambrogio, Kingston et al. — Nature Human Behaviour (human fMRI, ultrasound and computational experiments, November 16)

items.streamTitle: Proposing a group-specific word did not reliably strengthen human group identity
items.streamSummary: In 100 Japanese participants interacting with four disclosed LLM agents, proposing a neologism showed no reliable between-wave increase in collective identity; exploratory associations failed multiplicity correction.
items.attribution: Ito, Nagai, Wakamiya and Aramaki — Scientific Reports (human–AI group study, November 16)

items.streamTitle: Open inertial-sensor dataset synchronized wearable and object behavior observations
items.streamSummary: A November 16 Scientific Data descriptor released 50-person, 17-activity smart-home measurements from 30 synchronized wearable and object IMUs. It enables objective behavior measurement but does not establish intervention effects.
items.attribution: Sandhu, Lu, Kusy and Silvera-Tawil — Scientific Data (IMU-HAR-IL data descriptor, November 16)

items.streamTitle: More choices improved risk-task stability, but questionnaires remained more reliable
items.streamSummary: A November 15 behavioral measurement study found repeated choice items improved risk-preference reliability but established self-report scales retained better retest consistency; predictive validity remains a separate question.
items.attribution: Heinke, Schürmann, Andraszewicz et al. — Scientific Reports (risk-measurement comparison, November 15)

items.streamTitle: Randomly assigned AI peers shifted coding agents' rule-breaking decisions
items.streamSummary: A preregistered 420-team AI-agent experiment found deviant and honest scripted teammates shifted rule-breaking rates and norm statements. Its randomized findings concern model behavior, not a test of human social learning.
items.attribution: Ozer, Akgul and Chakravorty — arXiv preprint (preregistered multi-agent experiment, November 13)

items.streamTitle: Researchers uncovered an AI face-theft influence network targeting Canadians
items.streamSummary: An original November 12 investigation traced 293 TikTok/Instagram accounts, 3,201 face-stolen videos and 22.1 million plays; AI labeling detected only 4% of videos using real creator footage, without demonstrated audience effects.
items.attribution: Bridgman, Chan, Hobson et al. — Canadian Media Ecosystem Observatory (original incident investigation, November 12)

items.streamTitle: Initial human-versus-AI disclosure persisted despite hidden VR control changes
items.streamSummary: A 24-person within-subject VR experiment found initial human-versus-computer labels dominated perceived agency despite undisclosed control switches, while later actual behavior influenced social evaluations.
items.attribution: Zhang and Steed — arXiv preprint (human VR interaction experiment, November 9)

items.streamTitle: System personas shifted AI action thresholds under identical evidence
items.streamSummary: Across 20 LLMs and five million fixed-evidence decisions, changing ethical/cognitive persona prompts shifted affirmative-action rates across a 9.5-point range. This demonstrates AI prompt sensitivity, not human decision behavior.
items.attribution: Klang, Gorenshtein, Omar et al. — npj Health Systems (LLM prompt-controlled evaluation; 14 November 2026)

items.streamTitle: Source information and accuracy warnings reduced erroneous reliance on AI answers
items.streamSummary: An experiment with 800 adults found erroneous-answer acceptance fell from 45% without cues to 21% with both source information and warnings; 52% verified in the combined condition. Results concern low-risk, short-term AI-style judgments.
items.attribution: Xing, Zhang, Zhang et al. — Scientific Reports (randomized online experiment; 14 November 2026)

items.streamTitle: A 2019–2025 Hong Kong family-wellbeing dataset enables comparisons across disruptions
items.streamSummary: A Scientific Data release covers 7,744 Hong Kong respondents across 2019–2025 unrest, pandemic and recovery periods, with harmonized family-wellbeing variables. The data permit contextual comparisons but not automatic causal attribution.
items.attribution: Lam, Odetayo, Chan et al. — Scientific Data (multi-period public dataset descriptor; 14 November 2026)

items.streamTitle: Brain stimulation dissociated acquiring fear from maintaining it over a week
items.streamSummary: Human fear-conditioning research used EEG–fMRI and visual-cortex stimulation to find later memory retention could be disrupted while initial acquisition remained intact. The result concerns conditioned fear, not demonstrated narrative persuasion.
items.attribution: Brown, Ma, Wang et al. — Nature Communications (human neural stimulation and longitudinal retention; 14 November 2026)
